## Blocked, deliberately: `Bundle Analysis` red on a governance decision this seat cannot make

`domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`. Stating the blocker here on the PR rather than only on the card, so a reviewer landing on this page sees why it is red and why nothing is being pushed.

**Failing check:** `Bundle Analysis` (`100528606288`) on `5ad78fde`. Every other check is green or skipped.

```
❌ Console Performance Budget                     Status: FAIL
  Aggregate closure ceiling        ✅ pass    3178.3 KB / 3191.4 KB
  Per-chunk ceilings               ❌ over its ceiling
  Ceiling sensitivity (headroom)   ✅ pass
  Ceiling freshness                ✅ pass
```

| chunk | before | after | ceiling |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `framework` | 523,823 | **524,402** (+579) | 524,000 — **over by 402** |
| `ui-components` | 396,598 | 396,088 (−510) | 399,000 |
| aggregate eager closure | 3,254,604 | 3,254,620 (**+16**) | passes |

### It is this PR's byte cost, and it is still not this PR's to fix

The failure is real and attributable — I am not claiming otherwise. But the bytes are a **relocation, not growth**: the `framework` group is defined by path (`apps/console/vite.config.ts:742`, `/packages/(core|react|types)/`), so code moving *into* `packages/core` scores against it even though an equal amount left `ui-components`. This PR's true payload cost is **+16 bytes across a 3.25 MB closure**, and the aggregate ceiling passes. CI's own package table shows both halves: `fields` 61.71 → 61.26 KB gz, `core` 2.32 → 2.42 KB gz.

The relocation is not optional. The ruling on #7178 requires routing through the date path list cells already use and forbids a second date convention; `packages/core` is the React-free engine and cannot import from `packages/fields`, so the shared `formatDate` / `formatDateTime` had to move down — the same move objectui#4576 made for `formatDisplayNumber`.

### What I am NOT doing, and why

- ⛔ **Not raising `PER_CHUNK_GZIP_CEILINGS.framework`.** A gate ceiling is the maintainer's call and is the open subject of #7399. Raising it to fit my own PR is the one thing that card exists to prevent.
- ⛔ **Not shrinking the change to fit.** That means keeping a date convention inside `dataset-format.ts` — the second-convention failure the ruling and #4576 both forbid. It would trade a governance blocker for exactly the defect this card exists to fix.
- ⛔ **Not re-running the check.** This is a deterministic budget computation, not a flake: it reproduces on two full local builds with CI's own recipe and on CI. A re-run would return the identical number and burn a runner for nothing. The re-run allowance exists for a failure that might not reproduce; this one will.
- ⛔ **No test skipped, disabled or quarantined.** No baseline re-pinned, no budget script touched.

### Where it goes

Parked behind **#7399** (the open `framework` ceiling decision), alongside #7391 and #7400 — this is now the third PR blocked there. New evidence posted to #7399 at [5520783051](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/7399#issuecomment-5520783051): this PR is the first case where the gate reds on a change whose aggregate cost is +16 bytes, which is a property of how the per-chunk ceiling *attributes* bytes rather than of the change.

Full review of the implementation — including the one place the ruling's pin is **not literally satisfiable** for `datetime`, and why option A was taken anyway — is on the card at [5520776537](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/7178#issuecomment-5520776537). The PR stays **draft**; auto-merge is not enabled and it has not been enqueued.

## ✅ Unblocked — the ceiling this was parked behind is fixed. `main` merged in; landing once green.

`domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`. Retiring the "Blocked, deliberately" notice above ([5520817103](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/pull/7442#issuecomment-5520817103)) — its blocker no longer holds.

**#7399 was ruled** (maintainer, 2026-09-03, option **A′**) and landed as `177afeba1` (PR #7489). The `framework` chunk was **78.7% `@object-ui/i18n` locale catalogue**, because `framework` and `infrastructure` tied at priority 80 and `framework` was written first. The catalogue now has its own `i18n-locales` chunk and both ceilings were re-baselined in the same change.

### ⭐ This PR's own analysis was right, and the fix vindicates it

That notice argued the failure was **attribution, not growth**:

> the bytes are a **relocation, not growth** … This PR's true payload cost is **+16 bytes across a 3.25 MB closure**, and the aggregate ceiling passes.

That was correct, and it was correct for a deeper reason than the notice knew: the ceiling it tripped was not budgeting `core|react|types` at all. `framework` now measures ~60 KB against a **71,000** ceiling (baseline 61,465), where before it measured 523,823 against 524,000 — **41 bytes of headroom for the whole repository**. This PR's +579 B fits with room to spare.

⚠️ For the record, and against my own earlier reasoning: I later argued on several PRs that a red here could be diagnosed from the path rule (`/packages/(core|react|types)/`). **That rule is false in this repo** — it names the chunk but not its contents — and I published three wrong causal stories from it before the measurement settled the question. The full retraction is on #7399. This PR's notice reasoned better than I did about its own failure.

### What I did

Merged `main` in so CI rebuilds against the new grouping. ⛔ No ceiling was raised, ⛔ nothing was shrunk to fit, ⛔ no re-run spent — exactly as that notice promised.

⇒ Once every check is green by name, this seat lands it. The implementation review stands on the card ([#7178 comment 5520776537](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/7178#issuecomment-5520776537)), including the one place the ruling's pin is not literally satisfiable for `datetime` and why option A was taken anyway.
